chunk_findings.detail: `item.completed` previously listed only `"changelog"` (a `str`) and `"evidence"` (a `list[str]`). This change appends `"not_applicable"`, whose value is a `dict[str, str]` (from `_na_map`), i.e. a container of free text that the redactor has never seen at this field. The intent states these reasons are to be "redact[ed] as log free text". Given an excusal whose reason contains a secret, e.g. `Verdict.na_evidence = ["security: bypassed with token [REDACTED]"]`, the writer emits `not_applicable = {"security": "bypassed with token [REDACTED]"}`. Nothing in this diff changes the redactor to walk a dict-of-strings: if the walker redacts per-name by checking `isinstance(v, str)` or by iterating `for s in v` (which on a dict yields the *keys*), the reason strings — the only sensitive part — pass through verbatim, and the secret is persisted/printed unredacted; if instead the walker assumes a scalar/list and calls `v.split(...)` or a regex on it, it raises `TypeError` and the completion write/redaction path fails. Either the new dict shape must be added to the redactor's handled shape (redacting the dict's values), or the field must not be advertised as a plain free-text field here. The stated intent ("redact as log free text") is not kept by this diff alone.

chunk_findings.detail: The diff for this change contains only the added test; no hunk touches `ddflow/core/redact.py`, the `item.completed` payload emitter, the `ddflow show` completion ledger, or `gates_ahead_of`/`check_order`, even though the stated intent is precisely to add those. The new test exercises behavior this change does not implement: it calls `R.redact_event_data("item.completed", {"not_applicable": {...}}, red)` and asserts both that the `sk-…` secret is gone and that the nested key set is preserved. Unless the existing log-policy path of `redact_event_data` already recurses into arbitrary nested mappings under an unknown new key and treats them as log free text, the nested reason is returned unredacted and the first assertion (`"[REDACTED]" not in str(out)`) fails; conversely, if the implementation that would make this pass is not in this change, the test is red on the current tree. The sibling assertions described in the intent — `not_applicable` appearing additively in `item.completed`, being rendered in the `show` ledger, and the lazy diff being threaded into `gates_ahead_of`/`check_order` so a diff-excused required gate is not reported "ahead" — have no corresponding source hunks and no test coverage in this diff at all, so the feature as described is unverified and unimplemented here.
